lines.text: A contractor's last day.
You remove their Payroll access.
They still have it.
Because access is never just one grant.
It flows through groups inside groups.
Through service accounts, and on-call rotations.
Through a break-glass account nobody remembers.
Five routes. One person.
And some access has to stay.
Their training. Their data warehouse. Their pager.
Cut the wrong edge, and someone else stops working.
This is AccessCut.
An agent plans the cut. A graph checks every step.
First, FalkorDB finds every route.
The agent proposes a plan.
It's rejected. The warehouse access would be lost, and the graph says which edges caused it.
So the agent swaps one edge.
One route is still open. It adds one more.
Accepted.
Then, mid-run, someone adds a new grant.
The plan is now stale. Applying it is refused.
The agent looks again, and replans.
Six edges disabled, in one atomic write.
Payroll is gone. Everything else stays.
And the result comes from the graph, not from the model.
This is the live demo. Same agent. Real FalkorDB.
Sometimes there is no safe cut.
So it says so, shows why, and changes nothing.
Underneath, one traversal does the judging.
Every route. Every plan. Every check.
We tested it against an independent oracle.
Twenty-four of twenty-four. And fifteen of fifteen on scenarios it had never seen.
AccessCut.
Remove someone's access. Every route. Nothing else.
